items.text: An MSc in Physics, Chemistry, Biotechnology, or Data Science trains you to master one subject and generate original findings inside it.

blocks.heading: Use Four Questions for This Decision

items.text: The four questions narrows the decision to what matters for your specific situation.

When you picture the actual daily work five years from now, does it look like being the person who runs the experiment and defends the finding, or the person who decides what gets built, funded, or sold based on findings from other people.
Be honest about which version excites you on an ordinary Tuesday, not which one sounds better at a family function.

blocks.heading: Not the Brochure Number

items.text: Average MSc salaries in India commonly fall in a wide Rs 3-15 lakh range, with most fresh graduates starting closer to Rs 3-8 lakh a year depending on specialisation and location.
MBA outcomes vary far more by institute tier than MSc outcomes vary by university.

supporting: Average MSc salaries in India commonly fall in a wide Rs 3-15 lakh range, with most fresh graduates starting closer to Rs 3-8 lakh a year depending on specialisation and location. Within that range, data-science and statistics-linked MSc roles tend to sit toward the higher end, since demand for analytics skill currently outpaces the number of qualified candidates.

MBA outcomes vary far more by institute tier than MSc outcomes vary by university. Graduates from strong, well-ranked programs commonly move into roles in the Rs 10-25 lakh range, with consulting, analytics, and product-heavy placements running higher and top-tier institutes going well beyond that. Weaker or newer MBA programs, by contrast, often land outcomes that are not meaningfully different from a good MSc-plus-experience combination, while still costing two years of tuition and lost income to get there.

visuals.heading: Who Should Pivot to an MBA

items.text: Your real interest was always in how the science gets funded, sold, or scaled, not in generating the finding itself.
You want a faster, more predictable income timeline than a multi-year PhD stipend allows.
You are drawn to leading teams, making resourcing calls, or owning outcomes across functions rather than owning one narrow technical question.
You have already tested management-adjacent work, a lab-to-market project, a college fest, a part-time analyst stint, and it energised you more than the lab bench did.
